Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quick reference for procurement board (next Tue)

Hi Ava,

We're on a pretty tight timeline for Acme's procurement committee — they asked for 2-3 customer references to speak to our reliability and cost savings in the next procurement cycle. The board meeting is next Tuesday and the procurement lead asked if we can provide live references (15–20 min each).

Understand many vendors hear "reference fatigue" these days — customers are getting a lot of asks and it's become a logistic headache for us. Before I loop anyone, can you confirm:
- Who at Redwood can speak that week (availability window Tue/Wed next week)?
- Do you have substitutes or recorded testimonials if a live call won't work?
- Any short one-pager or FAQ we can share with the board ahead of the meeting?

If it's easier, feel free to propose a 10–15 minute recorded video or a short Q&A. Procurement is willing to accept recorded references if scheduling is impossible.

Appreciate quick confirmation — even a "yes we can/ here's fallback" is helpful.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Procurement, Acme Retail
sofia@acme-retail.com
[Attachment: acme_procurement_questions.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick reference for procurement board (next Tue)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up. Appreciated context, and totally understand the reference fatigue issue. Quick summary of options from our side: 

1) Live reference (preferred): Marcus can do a 20‑minute sync on Tues/Wed afternoon PST. He speaks to latency SLOs and the Dedicated deployment case.
2) Substituted reference: we can offer a short live call from a partner customer (BrightMart) — if procurement is OK with a comparable retail use-case rather than Acme peer.
3) Recorded testimonial or short video: 8–12 minutes recorded by our CS lead (Grace) focusing on ROI and operational notes.
4) Written Q&A / one‑pager: I can attach a concise reference one‑pager and a pre-populated Q&A to minimize lift.

If preference is to avoid live outreach to current customer contacts (to reduce fatigue), option 3 or 4 is quick and low-friction. I attached a one‑pager we can share directly with the board.

Bottom line: Marcus is available Tue 2/24 2–4pm PST or Wed 2/25 11am–2pm PST for a 20‑minute call. If none of those times work, we'll default to a recorded testimonial plus the one‑pager.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_reference_onepager.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]

Thanks Ava — I appreciate the quick options.

Unfortunately our procurement stakeholders are at back‑to‑back QBRs next week and several of the customer references you've offered have been asked recently by other vendors. We're trying to avoid pulling them into another live session (they flagged "reference fatigue" as a red flag).

Would Redwood be okay with a substituted contact? We have an independent consultant, Tom Nguyen at NorthCo (tom.nguyen@northco.com), who regularly helps our procurement team evaluate vendor fit; he'd be willing to vouch for operational fit and vendor responsiveness. He prefers a short call or a written Q&A.

If substitutes are allowed, we can schedule a 20‑minute call with Tom on Tue 3/2 at 10am PST. Alternately, the recorded testimonial + one‑pager would work and is probably the least disruptive for everyone.

I've attached the procurement team's questionnaire — it might help you tailor the Q&A.

Best,
Sofia
